reason: It survives the feasibility/schedule lens, but three of its gates need fixing before it runs. (1) Implementable, byte-identical when off, fail-soft. The forkmid splice point (tools/build_probe_kernel.py l.1777-1792: FORKMID_CALL goes just before the FINAL print inside filter_output_graph) still has repair_frame_cache in scope (exp58 post cell l.2001), and read_test_frame is defined in the same cell (l.139). So a FORKBLOB_ENABLE-gated call can read frames there with no new plumbing, and ENABLE=0 does not execute it. forkmid_edges is a pure function, so the harness can be copied, but the builder's ordering rule (l.2011-2018, forkmid last before safetail) has to be extended so that forkblob runs after forkmid. (2) Hidden-run cost is negligible. Frames are [64,256,256] uint16 = 8 MB, one blosc read is ~10-30 ms, and the crop blur is tiny. That is < 1 s/clip, ~1-2 min at N~100. step0.md puts K2's worst case at ~7.8 h against the 8.0 h DIVINS gate. forkblob runs after the insertion in each clip, so each later clip's gate check is delayed by <= ~1 s. The 12 h limit is not in play. (3) The lab can gate it. trainlab arms are graph-only replays of the exp60 dumps, and all 199 train zarrs are local (the prototype already reads them), so an arm costs ~1 h plus 0.5-1 h of CPU scoring. At 17:46Z exp60 has no results locally, so pre-registration is still clean. (4) Calendar: patch and tests tonight (~2.5 h), lab verdict on the morning of 26.09, K3 dummy ~0.5-0.7 GPU-h (~5 h of quota left after the exp60 shards; the weekly reset is expected Sat 00:00Z). S4 is 26.09 10:00-13:00, so the score lands ~18:00-21:00 26.09. S7 (27.09 <= 12:00, the R8 cutoff) is the fallback, and its score still arrives before S12 consolidation. The K3 submit needs the user's morning OK, since only K2 was pre-approved. Defects. (a) Dummy gate (2), 'count == prototype dose, 15 of 62', is ill-posed. K3's base is K2 (lowrefine + insertion + linefit move coordinates; the d2 note says the K2 dummy has 2 new non-inserted forks). In the prototype the 15 flagged forks are exactly the forks with sister <= 5.0 um: valley >= 0.95 never binds, and the minimum flagged valley is 0.959. Three forks sit just above the cut at 5.09, 5.20 and 5.30 um with valley ~1.0. The count will drift for benign reasons. (b) R3/R4 classification is ambiguous. R3's criterion is 'nodes unchanged' (C04 forkmid is listed there), but R4 covers 'changers of the node OR FORK set' and holds K3b (the DeepCenter threshold), which changes only forks. Under R4 forkblob would need +0.002 on public, far above its +0.001 central estimate. The class has to be fixed in writing before any score. (c) Bundling it with forkmid in one slot couples two riders whose lab P(pass) is only ~0.35-0.5 each. A K3 < K2 - 0.001 then kills both, and the result cannot be attributed. There are spare slots (S3 is held in branch A, S5 is free if K3b fails its gate, and S7 is left), so this is a design choice, not a schedule wall. Caveat: the thresholds come from GT sister statistics over all 151 train divisions, which include the lab's 99. No fork labels were seen, but the lab TP count is not fully blind.
fix: Before ANY `trainlab.py score` run (shard A alone included), append a timestamped CONTEXT line that pre-registers: s1 = 5.0 um, v1 = 0.95, sigma zyx (0.6,1.5,1.5), interior 20-80% of 41 samples, safe_division == 1 and not div_inserted forks only, run after forkmid; class = R3 (edge removal only, nodes identical, like C04), with its OWN lab gate (FP:TP >= 3 among the vetoed evaluable forks, <= 1 TP vetoed, div_J(arm) >= control on both halves, >= 10% of control forks in the cell); and the note that the thresholds used the GT stats of all train clips. Implement forkblob_edges(nodes_by_id, edges, frame_reader, s_um, v_min, sigma, scale) as a pure function with a crop margin >= 4 sigma, spliced after FORKMID_CALL, with builder ordering forkmid -> forkblob -> safetail. trainlab execs the SAME source with a train-zarr reader (no second copy, unlike forkmid). Unit tests: ENABLE=0 gives a CSV sha256 identical to K2; FORCE_FAIL gives 'FORKBLOB FAILED' with the input graph; on the exp56 dummy CSV the crop-blur valley matches the full-frame prototype within 0.005 and flags exactly the 15 forks. Replace dummy gate (2) with: nodes == K2; the removed-edge set equals the offline pure-function result on the K2 dummy's own final graph (not '15 of 62'); counters > 0 on 6bba_05db0fb1; no 'FORKBLOB FAILED'. Slotting: each rider enters K3 only if its own lab arm passes. If only forkblob passes, K3 = K2 + forkblob in S4. If both pass and a slot is free (S3 held or S5 unused), submit K2 + forkblob alone there so the two riders can be told apart. Otherwise use S7 (27.09 <= 12:00). Get the user's OK for the K3 submit in the morning.
realistic_gain: Feasibility: P(it reaches the LB before the R8 cutoff 27.09 12:00 | lab gate passes) ~0.85. P(lab gate passes) ~0.4-0.6, limited by how few evaluable forks the sparse labels give. Hidden-run cost is ~1-2 min at N~100, with >= 12 min margin to the 8.0 h DIVINS gate in the worst case. Agent cost ~4-5 h tonight, and it competes with T9 under R10. GPU cost ~0.5-0.7 h for the K3 dummy. Expected shipped value is ~+0.0004-0.0006 public and ~+0.0003-0.0008 private, the idea's central +0.001 times P(gate). Value itself is for the value lens to judge.
